Theme

Travel & transport · Nature & food

eastern adjective

also east (as in the east side), easterly, in the east, facing east, Eastern (of the East), oriental

post-classical

Just. 14.2.8; Gell. 2.22.11: ventī (Lewis & Short)
Aug. Conf. 9.7.15: orientālium partium
Traupman 203, 308

orientālis, orientāle

eastern, of the East

The adjective of oriēns, the east (see east): post-classical (Justin, Gellius), but the plain word, and Augustine’s for the Christians of the East. Classical prose has no adjective for it and says it with the noun.

Other words

  • ad orientem — to the east, facing east

    preposition with accusative · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.66: ab oriente ad occidentem (Lewis & Short, s.v. orior)

    The classical way: ad orientem spectāre, to face east, as Cato’s in merīdiem spectet for south (see southern); quae ad orientem sunt, the eastern parts.

Examples

  • tunc hymnī et psalmī ut canerentur secundum mōrem orientālium partium, nē populus maerōris taediō contābēsceret, īnstitūtum est

    it was then laid down that hymns and psalms should be sung after the custom of the eastern regions, so that the people should not waste away in weary griefAug. Conf. 9.7.15

See also east, east wind, southern, northern.
